correctness.rationale: For a fixed tree, the source/sink indicator pair covariance is negative at one vertex, positive and exactly 2^{-d(u)-d(v)} at an adjacent ordered pair, and zero at nonadjacent vertices; this reconstructs the degree formula. A completion-of-squares identity produces the edge energy; a leaf-count inequality handles four or more leaves, and a unique cubic vertex analysis gives the sharp 13/64 bound and iff equality at three leaves. Direct exhaustive edge-orientation checks and exact rational Prüfer enumeration in verify.py returned VERIFY_OK 71605 assertions. Finite checks corroborate rather than prove the infinite statement.

value.rationale: The joint dependence between source and sink counts on a randomly oriented tree is intrinsic to network directionality. The all-tree optimum has a universal nonzero shape-stability gap of 13/64, and the complete second-best family realizes it for every order at least seven; this is a precise structural statement neither dictated by marginal sink counts nor merely a single finite instance. The covariance also changes sign along paths as order increases.
